paragraphs.text: The Company says that it uses some custom components that are not commonly used by its competitors, and that new products often use custom components available from only one source. It also warns that component suppliers may decide to concentrate on producing common components instead of components customized to meet the Company’s requirements, which could further limit its ability to obtain sufficient quantities of components on commercially reasonable terms, or at all. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0004]

In context, the filing suggests the Company prefers or relies on customized components for certain products because they help meet its requirements, while a shift by suppliers toward common components would be a supply-risk issue rather than a benefit to the Company’s operating model. The disclosure does not say the Company itself is choosing common components over customized ones; it says suppliers might make that choice, which could constrain supply. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0004]

judge.label: PARTLY_RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer is responsive to the question and is supported in part by the filing evidence: it states that suppliers may concentrate on common components instead of components customized to the Company’s requirements, which could limit supply. However, the candidate adds unsupported or potentially misleading details about the Company using custom components not commonly used by competitors and new products using components available from only one source. Those points are not clearly supported by the provided reference evidence, so the answer is only partly supported.

paragraphs.text: The Company says research and development is central to competitiveness because the industries it competes in are marked by rapid technological advances, so its ability to compete successfully “depends heavily” on maintaining a continual and timely flow of competitive products, services, and technologies to the marketplace. It adds that it continues to develop new technologies to enhance existing offerings and expand its range through R&D, licensing of intellectual property, and acquisitions of third-party businesses and technology. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0005]

The Company also frames innovation as a broader competitive requirement, stating that its ability to compete successfully depends heavily on the continuing and timely introduction of innovative new products, services, and technologies. In that discussion, the Company links competition to product and service features, design and technology innovation, and the ability to keep introducing new offerings in fast-moving markets. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0003]

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer is responsive to the question and supported by the filing evidence. It accurately states that the Company views R&D as critical to competitiveness because fast technological change requires a continual and timely flow of competitive products, services, and technologies, and that the Company uses R&D to develop new technologies and expand offerings. The added discussion of innovation is also consistent with the filing’s emphasis on maintaining competitive products and services.

paragraphs.text: A stronger U.S. dollar could reduce the U.S. dollar value of the Company’s foreign currency–denominated sales and earnings. The filing says that if the Company does not raise international pricing to offset U.S. dollar strengthening, that would adversely affect the U.S. dollar value of the gross margins it earns on those sales. In other words, a stronger dollar can compress reported gross margins on foreign-currency sales when local prices are not increased enough to compensate. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0034] [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0035]

The filing also indicates that foreign exchange fluctuations can affect gross margins more broadly through pricing and cost channels. It states that gross margins are subject to downward pressure from fluctuations in foreign exchange rates, and that hedging with foreign currency forward and option contracts may not fully offset adverse movements. It also notes that foreign-currency strength can increase the cost of product components denominated in those currencies, further reducing gross margins. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0033] [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0035]

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer directly addresses the question and is supported by the cited filing evidence. It also reasonably adds that FX movements and hedging/cost effects can further pressure gross margins.

paragraphs.text: Foreign currency hedging may fail to fully offset adverse exchange-rate moves because the Company says its derivative hedges cover only “certain exposures” and “may not be effective to offset any, or more than a portion, of the adverse financial effects” of unfavorable currency movements, especially “over the limited time the hedges are in place.” [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0035]

The filing also indicates that hedging is only one part of a broader foreign-exchange response: the Company may choose not to raise international pricing for competitive or other reasons, and strengthening foreign currencies can still lead to lower pricing, derivative losses, or higher component costs. Those business choices and cost pressures can leave some exchange-rate exposure unhedged or reduce the benefit of the hedge. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0034]

paragraphs.text: The filing says the company is exposed to write-down risk on inventory and other assets when product and component inventories become obsolete, exceed anticipated demand, or have cost above net realizable value. It also says the company reviews long-lived assets and records impairment/write-downs if carrying value exceeds fair value, and that rapid, unpredictable product obsolescence could lead to write-downs, fees, impairments, and other charges. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0013]

For purchase commitments, the company says it accrues cancellation fee reserves for orders of excess products and components and faces risk that it may not fully utilize firm purchase commitments. The filing explains that because markets are volatile, competitive, and subject to rapid technology and price changes, the company may forecast incorrectly and order or produce excess or insufficient amounts of components or products, which could leave it unable to use committed purchases fully. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0013, 0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0014]

On excess or insufficient components or products, the filing specifically ties the risk to forecast error: the company orders components and builds inventory in advance, but if it misjudges demand it may end up with excess stock, shortages, or underused firm purchase commitments. The consequence described is inventory and commitment-related charges, including cancellation fee reserves and possible write-downs or other losses from obsolete or overvalued inventory. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0013]

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The candidate answer is responsive to the question and supported by the reference evidence. It accurately identifies the described risks: inventory write-downs for obsolete/excess inventory or cost above net realizable value, purchase commitment cancellation fee reserves for excess orders, and the risk of forecasting incorrectly and ordering or producing excess or insufficient components or products. It also notes possible related charges from rapid product obsolescence, which is consistent with the filing evidence.

paragraphs.text: The company says rapid and unpredictable product obsolescence can cause write-downs on inventory and other assets, including capital assets held at suppliers’ facilities and inventory prepayments. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0013]

The company also says rapid product obsolescence can affect purchase commitments by causing it to forecast incorrectly, order or produce excess or insufficient amounts of components or products, and not fully utilize firm purchase commitments. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0013]

paragraphs.text: The company says forecasting component and manufacturing needs is difficult because its markets are volatile, highly competitive, and subject to rapid technology and price changes. [0000320193-24-000123:item-1a:0013]

The filing further explains that demand and supply conditions can shift quickly due to frequent new-product introductions, ramp-up issues, inventory and purchase-commitment management, and the availability of products in the right quantities and at expected costs. The Company states that it believes it complies with the DMA and has been adjusting its compliance plan in response to the Commission’s feedback and engagement.

paragraphs.text: Apple says it uses derivatives to manage both foreign exchange and interest rate exposure. For foreign exchange risk, it may use forwards, options, cross-currency swaps, interest rate swaps, or other instruments, and it can designate them as cash flow hedges or fair value hedges depending on the exposure. It states that it generally hedges portions of forecasted foreign currency exposure tied to revenue and inventory purchases for up to 12 months, and it also uses derivatives that are not designated as accounting hedges to protect gross margins and offset foreign-currency remeasurement gains and losses on certain non-functional-currency assets and liabilities. [0000320193-24-000123:item-8:0010] [0000320193-24-000123:item-8:0011]

For interest rate exposure, Apple says it may use interest rate swaps, options, or other instruments to protect term debt or marketable securities from changes in interest rates, again designating these instruments as cash flow or fair value hedges. It also specifically discloses that, on certain U.S. dollar-denominated fixed-rate notes, it uses interest rate swaps to effectively convert fixed rates to floating rates, and on certain foreign-currency-denominated notes it uses cross-currency swaps to effectively convert those notes to U.S. dollar-denominated notes. [0000320193-24-000123:item-8:0011] [0000320193-24-000123:item-8:0019]

Apple also discloses control and scope limits around hedging: it may choose not to hedge certain exposures for accounting reasons or because the economic cost would be prohibitive, and there is no assurance the hedges will offset more than a portion of the financial impact from foreign exchange or interest rate movements. The filing further shows the scale of outstanding derivative positions, including foreign exchange contracts designated as accounting hedges, foreign exchange contracts not designated as accounting hedges, and interest rate contracts. [0000320193-24-000123:item-8:0010] [0000320193-24-000123:item-8:0011]

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer is responsive to the question and is supported by the cited filing evidence. It also accurately notes the use of non-designated derivatives to protect gross margins and offset certain foreign-currency remeasurement effects. The answer includes some details beyond the excerpted evidence, but nothing is contradicted and the core explanation is well supported.

paragraphs.text: Uncertain tax positions are tax positions for which the company has not yet fully concluded whether the tax benefit will be sustained under applicable tax law. Apple says that, in accounting for some uncertain tax positions, it uses significant judgment in interpreting and applying GAAP and complex domestic and international tax laws, and auditors evaluate whether a position is “more likely than not” to be sustained and measure the amount of tax benefit that qualifies for recognition. In other words, these are tax treatments whose ultimate acceptance by tax authorities is not certain. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0028]

Apple disclosed that, as of September 27, 2025, its gross unrecognized tax benefits were $23.2 billion, with $10.6 billion that would affect the effective tax rate if recognized. It also noted that tax years remain open to examination in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and certain foreign jurisdictions, and that gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease by as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months. These disclosures show that uncertain tax positions create material risk around the amount and timing of tax expense and potential future adjustments. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0016]

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer is responsive to the question and supported by the filing evidence. It explains that uncertain tax positions are tax positions whose tax benefits may not be fully sustained under applicable law, and cites the company’s use of significant judgment and the ‘more likely than not’ recognition standard. That aligns with the reference evidence describing evaluation of uncertain tax positions, their technical merits, and the measurement of benefits that qualify for recognition.

paragraphs.text: Auditing management’s evaluation of uncertain tax positions can be complex because the judgments depend on whether each tax position is “more likely than not to be sustained” and on measuring the tax benefit that qualifies for recognition. The filing says these assessments require significant judgment and are based on interpretations of tax laws, including complex domestic and international tax laws. 【0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027】【0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0028】

The complexity is also heightened by the scale and scope of the company’s positions: as of September 27, 2025, gross unrecognized tax benefits were $23.2 billion, with $10.6 billion that would affect the effective tax rate if recognized, and the company is subject to tax in the U.S. and numerous foreign jurisdictions. The filing also notes that tax years remain open to examination in multiple jurisdictions and that the timing of resolution is uncertain, which adds to audit difficulty. 【0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027】【0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0016】

In short, auditors must evaluate technical tax-law interpretations, management’s assumptions and analysis, and the measurement of uncertain benefits across many jurisdictions, all of which involve subjective judgments and unresolved tax matters. The auditor’s procedures described in the filing reflect that challenge, including testing controls, reviewing management’s analysis, and involving tax subject-matter resources to assess the technical merits of positions. 【0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0028】【0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027】

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The candidate answer directly addresses why auditing management’s evaluation of uncertain tax positions can be complex: it cites the need to judge whether positions are more likely than not to be sustained, measure the tax benefit to recognize, interpret complex domestic and international tax laws, and handle significant judgment and unresolved tax matters across jurisdictions. These points are supported by the reference evidence.

paragraphs.text: The auditors treated uncertain tax positions as a critical audit matter and said they addressed it by testing controls over management’s evaluation of whether tax positions were more likely than not to be sustained, the measurement of the related tax benefits, and the disclosures. They also evaluated the Company’s assessment and measurement of the tax benefit that qualified for recognition. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0028]

In addition, the audit procedures included reading and evaluating management’s assumptions and analysis and, where applicable, the Company’s communications with taxing authorities to understand the basis and technical merits of the uncertain tax positions. The auditors also involved tax subject matter resources to assess the technical merits of certain positions based on their knowledge of relevant tax laws and experience with related taxing authorities, and they evaluated the related Note 7 disclosures. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0028]

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer is responsive and well supported by the reference evidence. It accurately describes the auditors’ procedures for uncertain tax positions: testing related controls, evaluating management’s assessment and measurement of positions, reviewing assumptions, analysis and communications with taxing authorities, involving tax subject matter experts, and checking the disclosures.

The company also says its products include operating systems, server applications, business solution applications, software development tools, desktop and server management tools, and video games. In addition, Microsoft says it designs and sells devices such as PCs, tablets, gaming and entertainment consoles, other intelligent devices, and related accessories.

In describing its operating model, Microsoft says it is a technology company founded in 1975 that develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions to deliver value for customers and help people and businesses realize their full potential. paragraphs.text: Expanding vertically integrated capabilities could help Microsoft compete by allowing it to offer a more complete hardware-software-services package, which the filing says can create a vertically integrated model that has succeeded in consumer products and may provide security and performance benefits. The filing also notes that Microsoft already offers some vertically integrated products and services, so expansion could strengthen that approach, but the same disclosure warns it could increase costs, reduce margins, and create operational risks. [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0001]

The filing also suggests that greater vertical integration could support Microsoft’s efforts to build scale and maintain its ecosystem competitiveness, since it says significant marketplace scale is necessary to meet demand and sustain attractive margins. At the same time, competing platform ecosystems and marketplaces are described as making it harder to attract and retain customers and developers, so expanding vertically integrated capabilities could be a way to reinforce customer appeal and ecosystem strength while accepting higher cost and margin pressure. [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0000] [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0002]

judge.label: RELEVANT

paragraphs.text: Microsoft says its PC operating systems depend on application-developer participation because platform ecosystems create network effects among users, developers, and the platform provider, and “to compete successfully, we must enlist developers to write applications for our platform.” It also says competing platforms have their own content and application marketplaces with scale and significant installed bases, which makes the variety and utility of apps an important factor in device purchasing decisions. [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0000] [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0002]

The rise of smartphones and tablets can make this harder because Microsoft says users increasingly turn to these devices for functions that used to be performed by PCs, and these devices compete on price and utility. paragraphs.text: Rival platform-based ecosystems could make it harder for Microsoft to attract and retain customers because competing platforms can build network effects among users, developers, and the platform provider, and “firms offering competing platforms may make it more difficult to attract and retain customers.” The filing also says that establishing significant scale is necessary to meet consumer demand and maintain attractive margins, implying that rivals with larger ecosystems can strengthen their position and make Microsoft’s platform less attractive. [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0000]

The filing further explains that competing platforms with large content and application marketplaces and significant installed bases influence device purchasing decisions because the variety and utility of available content and applications matter to users. It also notes that users may face costs to move data and buy new content and applications when switching platforms, which can increase lock-in to rival ecosystems and make customer retention more difficult for Microsoft. [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0002]

Microsoft says it must enlist developers to write applications for its own platform and ensure those applications are high quality, secure, customer appealing, and valuable. The filing adds that competitors’ rules for their marketplaces may limit Microsoft’s ability to distribute products and services through them as it would like, which can hinder customer acquisition and engagement on rival-controlled ecosystems. [0001193125-26-323660:item-1a:0002]

judge.label: RELEVANT

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says it is unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China’s data center market because U.S. export controls applicable to China are “complex” and measure multiple chip characteristics, including total processing performance, performance density, interconnect bandwidth, and memory bandwidth. NVIDIA says these measures can make licenses burdensome, temporary, or unavailable, and can benefit competitors while encouraging customers to seek alternatives. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0047; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0048]

The filing further says China’s Action Plan could set compute-performance-per-watt and memory-bandwidth standards for data centers that would prevent NVIDIA from designing products to meet the new standard, even if U.S. controls changed, thereby restricting customers’ ability to use some NVIDIA data center products. It further states that these fair value changes would be offset in total other income, net, by corresponding changes in fair value of foreign-currency-denominated monetary assets and liabilities, assuming the hedge contracts fully cover those balances. paragraphs.text: Uncertain tax positions are tax positions the company has taken that may not ultimately be sustained under audit or legal review, so Apple measures and discloses the associated tax benefit only to the extent management believes the position is more likely than not to be sustained and can be recognized under GAAP. The filing says that, in accounting for some of these positions, Apple uses significant judgment in interpreting and applying GAAP and complex domestic and international tax laws. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0028]

As of September 27, 2025, Apple reported $23.2 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits, and $10.6 billion of that amount would affect the effective tax rate if recognized. The company also reported that the balance of gross unrecognized tax benefits changed from $22.0 billion at September 28, 2024 to $23.242 billion at September 27, 2025, with increases from current- and prior-year tax positions partly offset by settlements and statute expirations. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0016] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027]

The filing indicates that these tax positions can move materially over time because their resolution is uncertain: tax years 2018 and after 2021 for the U.S. federal jurisdiction, and after 2014 in certain major foreign jurisdictions, remained subject to examination, and Apple said it was reasonably possible gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease by as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months. The filing also describes a separate tax risk event tied to the European Commission State Aid Decision, under which the ECJ confirmed the Commission’s 2016 decision and Apple recorded a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion net in the fourth quarter of 2024. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0016] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0014]

Interpretation: in plain English, uncertain tax positions are disputed or judgment-heavy tax positions whose ultimate acceptance by tax authorities is not certain, so the company carries a liability-like balance for the portion it has not recognized and discloses how much of that balance could change earnings or the effective tax rate. For Apple, the disclosed material risk is that tax authorities or courts could later challenge or accept positions in ways that would significantly alter tax expense, cash taxes, and the effective tax rate. [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0027] [0000320193-25-000079:item-8:0016]

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is built around GPUs, and the filing says these GPUs are the foundation because they excel at parallel workloads such as training and inferencing neural networks. The filing further says the platform is available in NVIDIA’s own accelerated computing platform and in industry-standard servers from major cloud providers and server makers. The software side of the platform includes the CUDA parallel programming model, the CUDA-X collection of acceleration libraries, APIs, SDKs, and domain-specific application frameworks. NVIDIA also says its data center computing platform includes NVIDIA AI Enterprise software, DGX Cloud, and a growing body of acceleration libraries, APIs, SDKs, and domain-specific application frameworks; elsewhere it describes NeMo as a complete solution for building enterprise-ready large language models. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0005][0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0010]

The filing also identifies additional software and platform products associated with NVIDIA’s accelerated computing approach: NVIDIA vGPU software for graphics-rich virtual desktops and workstations, GeForce Experience, Studio drivers, NVIDIA Avatar Cloud Engine (ACE), and Omniverse. NVIDIA describes Omniverse as a development platform and operating system for building virtual world simulation applications, and also as real-time 3D design collaboration and virtual world simulation software. In automotive, the filing says DRIVE Hyperion includes the DRIVE AGX hardware, a reference sensor set, and an open, modular DRIVE software platform, while NVIDIA DRIVE Sim is a data center-based simulation solution based on Omniverse software. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0005][0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0011][0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0008]

[0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0000][0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0004][0001045810-24-000029:item-1:0005]

paragraphs.text: Direct filing fact: NVIDIA says the export controls applicable to China are complex and address multiple chip parameters, including total processing performance, “performance density,” interconnect bandwidth, and memory bandwidth. NVIDIA further states that, under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, it is unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China’s data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government, and that as of the end of fiscal year 2026 it was effectively foreclosed from competing in China’s data center computing/compute market. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046]

Direct filing fact: the filing says the U.S. government has imposed worldwide export controls impacting NVIDIA’s products, and in January 2025 published the AI Diffusion IFR, which would have imposed a worldwide licensing requirement on data center products such as H200, GB200, and GB300, divided the world into three tiers, relegated most countries to “Tier 2,” and created a complex and burdensome licensing scheme. The filing also says the U.S. government has already imposed license conditions that limit the ability of foreign firms to create and offer large-scale GPU clusters as a service, and may impose additional conditions such as chip tracking and throttling mechanisms that could disable or impair GPUs if unauthorized system configuration, use, or location is detected. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0047; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0048]

Direct filing fact: NVIDIA says China’s government has discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using its data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls. The filing also says a Chinese agency announced an Action Plan endorsing new standards for compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth of accelerators used in new and renovated data centers in China, and states that if U.S. controls changed to allow NVIDIA back into the market, China could modify or implement the Action Plan in a way that would effectively prevent NVIDIA from designing products to meet the new standard. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

Direct filing fact: NVIDIA says export controls targeting GPUs and semiconductors associated with AI may subject downstream users to restrictions on use, resale, repair, or transfer; may disrupt supply chain and distribution channels; may reduce demand outside China as well; and may encourage customers and overseas governments to “design-out” or prefer competitors’ products. The filing also says repeated changes in export-control rules impose compliance burdens and may lead to excess inventory or purchase obligations if products become restricted after development. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0042; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0043; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0050]

Interpretation: based only on the filing’s statements, the main barriers to a competitive China data-center product are a combination of U.S. export controls that constrain product specifications and licensing, plus Chinese market and regulatory conditions that can reject or discourage compliant U.S.-origin products. NVIDIA’s disclosed problem is not merely selling into China; it says it cannot simultaneously meet U.S. approval and Chinese government approval for a product that remains competitive in China’s data-center market. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

Interpretation: the specific export-control features that appear to constrain competitiveness are the filing’s references to performance ceilings and other technical thresholds, worldwide licensing requirements, license conditions limiting large-scale GPU clusters, and possible chip-tracking or throttling mandates. On the China side, the filing points to discouraged purchasing of U.S.-compliant or China-specific products and to Chinese compute standards that may be set in ways NVIDIA says it cannot meet while also satisfying the U.S. regime. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0047; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0048; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says its business is exposed to litigation, investigations, and regulatory proceedings, and that it currently faces and is likely to continue facing legal, administrative, and regulatory proceedings, claims, demands, and/or investigations involving shareholder, consumer, competition, and other issues relating to its business. It specifically discloses that it is defending a securities class action lawsuit brought by multiple shareholders alleging that NVIDIA and certain officers made false and/or misleading statements about channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand in 2017 and 2018. NVIDIA says adverse outcomes could include monetary damages, fines, injunctions stopping manufacturing or sales of certain products or business practices, compulsory patent licensing, or other remedies, and that any unfavorable outcome or settlement could have a material adverse impact. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058]

Interpretation: Based on the disclosed risk factors, NVIDIA appears to be exposed to at least four broad proceeding categories: shareholder litigation; consumer or competition-related claims or investigations; security/privacy-related regulatory inquiries or actions; and other unspecified legal, administrative, and regulatory matters tied to its business. The filing also highlights that security incidents, data privacy issues, and allegedly deficient privacy statements could trigger litigation, regulatory inquiries, enforcement actions, oversight, and fines, while corporate sustainability practices could draw additional scrutiny from shareholders, regulators, and others. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058] [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0023] [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0001] [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0047]

The filing also discloses exposure to regulatory proceedings connected to data privacy and security laws, including the possibility of government enforcement actions, additional reporting requirements and oversight, restrictions on processing data, and litigation if a security incident occurs or if privacy policies or statements are found deficient, deceptive, unfair, or misrepresentative. NVIDIA further notes that some European regulators have prevented companies from transferring personal data out of Europe for alleged GDPR cross-border transfer violations, and that its own customers’ contractual privacy requirements could, if not met, subject it to litigation, regulatory action, or fines. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0023] [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0054]

In addition, NVIDIA discloses exposure to regulatory constraints and proceedings arising from export controls. It says the U.S. government informed it on October 23, 2023 that licensing requirements were immediately effective for shipments of certain products to China, that it has not received licenses for those restricted products, and that the licensing process is time-consuming, uncertain, and may impose burdensome conditions. NVIDIA states these requirements have a disproportionate impact and have disadvantaged, and may continue to disadvantage, it relative to competitors. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0043]

limitations: The supplied evidence does not include the full Item 1A section, so this answer is limited to the proceedings and risks expressly mentioned in the provided excerpts.

No separate list of all actual pending lawsuits, government investigations, or named regulators was provided beyond the securities class action and the general references to regulatory actions, inquiries, enforcement, and oversight.
The excerpts do not establish the current status, timing, jurisdiction, or merits of any proceeding beyond what is quoted here.

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The candidate answer is responsive to the question and supported by the reference evidence. It correctly states that NVIDIA says it is exposed to litigation, investigations, and regulatory proceedings involving shareholder, consumer, competition, and other issues, and it accurately mentions the specifically disclosed securities class action related to channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining demand. It also stays broadly consistent with the filing’s language about possible adverse outcomes and remedies. Some added details about privacy, security, and export controls are not in the provided reference excerpt, but they do not contradict it.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA discloses that, in litigation and regulatory proceedings, adverse rulings could include monetary damages or fines, an injunction stopping it from manufacturing or selling certain products, an order preventing certain business practices, or other remedies such as compulsory licensing of patents. It also says that an unfavorable outcome or settlement may result in a material adverse impact. The filing further states that, regardless of outcome, litigation can be costly, time-consuming, and disruptive to operations. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058]

For IP-related disputes specifically, the filing says an unfavorable ruling could include significant damages, invalidation of one or more patents, indemnification of third parties, payment of lost profits, or injunctive relief. If NVIDIA or an indemnitee cannot obtain a needed license on acceptable terms or at all, it could face substantial liabilities or have to suspend or discontinue the manufacture and sale of one or more products, and it may need to make royalty or other payments or cross-license technology. The filing also says indemnification of a customer or other indemnitee may increase operating expenses and negatively impact operating results. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0049]

In practical terms, the disclosed downside from an unfavorable legal outcome or settlement could therefore include direct monetary costs, operational limits on specific products or business practices, licensing or royalty obligations, and management diversion, with the company stating these matters could materially and adversely affect financial results and operations. This is interpretation drawn only from the cited risk-factor language; the filing does not quantify the likelihood or size of any particular case outcome. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058; 0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0049]

limitations: The supplied evidence provides general risk-factor disclosures and one example of a securities class action, but it does not provide case-specific facts about any actual settlement amount, probability, timing, or which proceeding would produce which remedy.
The evidence is limited to excerpts from Item 1A and does not include procedural posture, pleadings, court rulings, or settlement terms for the referenced proceedings.

judge.label: RELEVANT

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA discloses that its indebtedness could adversely affect its financial position and cash flows from operations, and could prevent it from implementing its strategy or fulfilling contractual obligations. The company says that as of January 28, 2024, it had net outstanding $9.7 billion in notes due by 2060, and that as each series of senior notes matures it must repay or refinance the notes unless redeemed or repurchased. It also states it has a $575 million commercial paper program. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058]

The filing also warns that if NVIDIA chooses to refinance its notes, it may receive less favorable terms or may be unable to refinance at all, which could adversely affect its financial condition. In addition, maintaining current and future indebtedness and related contractual restrictions could cause NVIDIA to dedicate a substantial portion of cash flows from operations to debt service and principal repayments, reduce flexibility, impair future financing access, and restrict business actions such as granting liens, entering mergers, disposing of assets, or materially changing the business. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0059]

If covenants in the indenture are breached without a waiver, the filing says outstanding indebtedness may be declared immediately due and payable, which could intensify liquidity pressure and cash outflow needs. The company also states that changes to its credit rating may negatively affect the value and liquidity of its securities, restrict future financing, and alter the terms of any such financing. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0059]

Interpretation: Taken together, the disclosed debt and maturities could pressure NVIDIA’s future cash flows because principal repayments or refinancing would require cash at maturity dates extending through 2060, while ongoing debt service could reduce funds available for operations, investment, and other corporate uses. The filing further indicates that adverse refinancing terms, covenant breaches, or credit-rating deterioration could make financing more expensive or less available, potentially weakening financial flexibility and increasing refinancing risk. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058; 0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0059]

limitations: The evidence discloses the amount of notes due by 2060 and the company’s stated risk factors, but it does not provide a maturity schedule by series, interest rates, or specific covenant terms.
The filing states potential effects in risk-factor language; it does not quantify future cash flow impact, refinancing costs, or likelihood of covenant breach.

It also reasonably explains the implications for liquidity, financial flexibility, and cash available for operations, which are consistent with the filing’s risk-factor language.

limitations: The evidence provided states the total valuation allowance, but does not break out the amount attributable specifically to capital loss carryforwards versus certain state and other deferred tax assets.

paragraphs.text: The filing says the company could recognize additional income tax expense or an income tax benefit if it changes its estimate of deferred tax assets and liabilities, including due to added certainty or finality to an anticipated outcome, changes in accounting standards or tax laws, or changes in other facts or circumstances. It also says the company may need to recognize such amounts if its assessment of potential U.S. or foreign income tax contingencies changes: if payment of recorded amounts is found unnecessary, or if the recorded tax liability is less than its current assessment, it may recognize an income tax benefit or additional income tax expense accordingly. [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0010]

The filing further indicates that realization of deferred tax assets could create an income tax benefit if those assets become more-likely-than-not to be realized. It also describes unrecognized tax benefits and related interest and penalties as sources of income tax expense, with the company recognizing a tax benefit only for positions that are more-likely-than-not to be sustained on audit. Separately, the IRS audit resolution in fiscal 2024 produced a non-cash net benefit, showing that settling tax positions can affect the tax line. [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0010] [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0016] [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0017] [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0020]

Interpretation: based only on this filing, the main triggers for additional tax expense or a tax benefit are changes in tax estimates, settlement or resolution of uncertain tax positions, reversals or realization of deferred tax assets, and changes in related interest/penalties. The filing does not provide a complete list of every possible accounting trigger, so this is a synthesis of the disclosed drivers rather than a comprehensive taxonomy. [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0010] [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0016] [0001045810-24-000029:item-7:0017]

limitations: The evidence is limited to selected MD&A excerpts from Item 7; it does not include the full tax footnote or all accounting policy details.

[0001045810-26-000021:item-7:0013]

paragraphs.text: The filing says the effective tax rate rose to 15.1% in fiscal 2026 from 13.3% in fiscal 2025 because there was a lower percentage of tax benefits from stock-based compensation, FDDEI, and the U.S. federal research tax credit relative to the increase in income before income tax. It also notes that both fiscal 2026 and 2025 rates were still below the 21.0% U.S. federal statutory rate due to tax benefits from FDDEI, stock-based compensation, income taxed at lower foreign rates, and the federal research tax credit. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7:0013]

Interpretation: the rate increase appears driven by the fact that pretax income grew faster than the tax benefits tied to equity compensation, FDDEI, and the research credit, so those benefits covered a smaller share of pretax earnings in fiscal 2026. The filing does not quantify each factor’s individual contribution, so the precise mix cannot be determined from this evidence alone. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7:0013]

limitations: The evidence provides only a single narrative explanation and does not break out the dollar or percentage impact of stock-based compensation, FDDEI, or the research tax credit separately.

No detailed tax footnote is included here, so the analysis cannot assess whether other items, such as the OBBBA or valuation allowance changes, affected the year-over-year effective tax rate beyond the stated primary reason.

This is supported by the cited filing language.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says the $8.5 billion of senior Notes create no financial statement risk from interest rate changes because the Notes “bear interest at a fixed rate,” and NVIDIA states that, for this reason, it has “no financial statement risk associated with changes in interest rates.” It also says the Notes are carried at “face value less unamortized discount” on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0000]

Interpretation: a fixed-rate debt instrument generally does not require periodic remeasurement of the recorded liability for market interest-rate moves in the way a variable-rate instrument might. On NVIDIA’s disclosure, the company’s reported statement is that the accounting carrying amount is not sensitive to rate changes, so the disclosed risk is a fair-value or economic risk rather than a financial-statement measurement risk. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0000]

limitations: The supplied evidence gives NVIDIA’s conclusion and one stated reason, but it does not include Note 11 or detailed accounting policy language explaining the measurement basis in more depth.
The evidence does not show whether there could be any off-balance-sheet, refinancing, or economic interest-rate exposure beyond the specific disclosure that there is no financial statement risk.

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The candidate answer is responsive and supported by the filing evidence. It correctly states NVIDIA’s reason: the senior Notes bear interest at a fixed rate, are carried at face value less unamortized discount, and therefore NVIDIA says it has no financial statement risk from interest rate changes. The added interpretation is reasonable and consistent with the disclosure.

paragraphs.text: The company says its direct exposure to foreign exchange rate fluctuations is minimal because substantially all of its sales are in U.S. dollars, and it uses foreign currency forward contracts to offset movements in foreign currency exchange rates. It also says gains or losses from foreign currency remeasurement are included in other income or expenses, and that the impact of foreign currency transaction gain or loss on net income was not significant for fiscal years 2026 and 2025. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0001]

The company further discloses that sales and arrangements with third-party manufacturers are priced and paid in U.S. dollars, so they are not subject to exchange rate fluctuations. It adds that a stronger U.S. dollar could make its products more expensive and hurt competitiveness, while a weaker U.S. dollar could cause suppliers to raise manufacturing costs. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0001]

On a sensitivity basis, the company estimates that a 10% strengthening of the U.S. dollar would have had an adverse pre-tax impact of $180 million on accumulated other comprehensive income related to foreign exchange contracts as of January 25, 2026, and $136 million as of January 26, 2025. It says the change in value of those contracts would be expected to offset the corresponding change in hedged forecasted foreign currency expenses when recognized. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0001]

The company also states that an adverse 10% foreign exchange rate change applied to its balance sheet hedging contracts would have resulted in a pre-tax adverse impact of $124 million as of January 25, 2026 and $129 million as of January 26, 2025. It says these fair value changes would be offset in total other income, net, by corresponding changes in the fair values of foreign currency denominated monetary assets and liabilities, assuming the hedge contracts fully cover those balances. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0001, 0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0002]

Interpretation: the disclosure presents foreign exchange risk as managed rather than material to current earnings, with hedging used to reduce exposure. However, the company still acknowledges some sensitivity in equity and income metrics under a hypothetical 10% U.S. dollar move, so the risk is not zero. [0001045810-26-000021:item-7a:0001]

limitations: The evidence is limited to Item 7A market-risk disclosure excerpts and does not include the underlying hedge note referenced by the filing.
The filing provides hypothetical sensitivity amounts, but not the full model assumptions or whether all foreign currency exposures are comprehensively hedged in practice.
No additional segment, geographic, or derivative note detail was provided beyond the cited excerpts.

judge.label: RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The candidate answer is directly responsive to the question and is well supported by the reference evidence. It accurately summarizes the company’s foreign exchange rate risk disclosure, including minimal direct exposure, use of forward contracts, U.S.-dollar pricing, and the stated sensitivity amounts for a 10% currency move.

paragraphs.text: The Company says that some component suppliers may decide to focus on producing common components rather than components customized to meet the Company’s requirements, and that this could further limit the Company’s ability to obtain sufficient quantities of components on commercially reasonable terms, or at all. It also states that it uses some custom components not commonly used by competitors, and that new products often rely on custom components available from only one source. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0004]

Because of that, a shift by suppliers toward common components could reduce supply flexibility and make it harder for Apple to secure needed parts on favorable terms. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0004][0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0005]

The filing also says the Company believes its intellectual property rights are important to differentiating its business, but that it relies primarily on the innovative skills, technical competence, and marketing abilities of its personnel. It adds that no single intellectual property right is solely responsible for protecting the Company’s products and services. [0000320193-25-000079:item-1:0005]

paragraphs.text: Apple says it supports employee feedback through an engagement approach built on open and honest communication: team members are encouraged to raise questions, feedback, or concerns with their managers, and the Company conducts surveys to gauge employee sentiment. Those surveys specifically assess issues such as career development, manager performance, and inclusivity. The filing also says Apple aims to create an inclusive, safe, and supportive environment and to foster equitable pay and access to opportunity for all employees.

In the broader human-capital context, Apple describes related programs that may reinforce this feedback-and-sentiment model, including leadership and management training through Apple University, online learning for business, technical, and personal development, and company efforts to increase diverse representation and sustain an inclusive workforce. However, the filing does not provide details on survey cadence, methodology, response rates, or how results are acted upon beyond the statement that surveys are conducted and employees are encouraged to communicate with managers.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says it cannot create and deliver a competitive product for China’s data center market because current U.S. export controls are complex and target multiple technical thresholds — including total processing performance, performance density, interconnect bandwidth, and memory bandwidth — and because, under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, it is unable to obtain approval from both the U.S. government and the Chinese government for a competitive China data center product. The filing also says NVIDIA was effectively foreclosed from China’s data center compute market, and that the U.S. government has imposed worldwide export controls that can affect its products beyond China. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046]

The filing further explains that export controls and related licensing rules can be broad and shifting, including a January 2025 AI Diffusion IFR that would have imposed a worldwide licensing requirement on NVIDIA data center products and divided countries into tiers, plus possible replacement rules that could add new restrictions or licensing requirements. It also says U.S. license conditions may limit foreign firms’ ability to create and offer large-scale GPU clusters, and could require chip-tracking or throttling mechanisms that may disable or impair GPUs; NVIDIA warns that these conditions can make pre-sale and post-sale support more cumbersome and less certain and can encourage customers to pursue competitors. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046] [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0047] [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0048]

NVIDIA also says the Chinese government has discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using its data center products, including China-specific products designed to comply with U.S. export controls, and has proposed or could implement standards on compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth for accelerators in Chinese data centers. NVIDIA warns that if U.S. controls ever changed to allow it back into China, China could still adopt or modify standards in a way that would prevent NVIDIA from designing products to meet them, which could block use of its data center products and harm its business. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

In summary, the disclosed barriers are: U.S. worldwide export controls on AI/GPU products; China-specific approval and licensing hurdles; technical thresholds based on performance, density, bandwidth, and memory bandwidth; possible license conditions such as chip tracking and throttling; and Chinese market restrictions or standards that discourage purchases and may make compliance-product design infeasible. NVIDIA states these combined restrictions leave it unable to deliver a competitive China data center product under current conditions. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046] [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0047] [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0048] [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

The answer goes somewhat beyond the provided excerpt with additional details about license conditions and Chinese restrictions, but these are consistent with the broader filing context and do not contradict the cited evidence.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says its inability to return to the China data center compute market could hurt it because China’s restrictions and standards may keep it from designing or selling a competitive product there, which would restrict customers’ ability to use some data center products and have a material adverse impact on business, operating results, and financial condition. The filing also says its effective foreclosure from China helped competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems, so a continued inability to re-enter could further strengthen rivals and worsen NVIDIA’s competitive position worldwide.

The filing adds that China has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged purchasing, importing, or using NVIDIA data center products, including China-specific products. It also says increased oversight of digital platform companies may adversely affect Data Center revenue, and that further restrictions could negatively affect business and financial results more broadly.

More generally, NVIDIA says export controls have already and could in the future reduce demand, disrupt supply chains and distribution channels, increase compliance burdens, and favor competitors that are less likely to be restricted. The filing notes these controls can hurt markets outside China too and can even lead customers to design out U.S. semiconductors, which would further pressure revenue and financial condition.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says its indebtedness could adversely affect its financial position and cash flows from operations, and could also prevent it from implementing its strategy or fulfilling contractual obligations. The company states that it had $9.7 billion in notes outstanding due by 2060 as of January 28, 2024, and that each series of senior notes must be repaid or refinanced when it matures unless redeemed or repurchased. If refinancing is needed, NVIDIA says it may obtain less favorable terms or may be unable to refinance at all, which could adversely affect its financial condition. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058]

The filing also warns that maintaining current and future indebtedness and related contractual restrictions could consume a substantial portion of cash flows from operations for debt service and principal repayments. NVIDIA says this could increase vulnerability to adverse economic, industry, and competitive changes; limit flexibility to change its business; impair access to future financing; and restrict actions such as granting liens, entering mergers, disposing of assets, or materially changing the business. It also says covenant breaches could cause outstanding indebtedness to become immediately due and payable, and that credit rating changes could hurt the value and liquidity of its securities and affect future financing terms. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0059]

In practical terms, the disclosed risk is that debt service and refinancing obligations through 2060 could reduce cash available for operations and strategic investment, while refinancing or covenant problems could worsen financial condition or force accelerated repayment. The filing does not quantify the likely future cash burden or specify when, beyond the stated maturities, the impact would be greatest. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0058

limitations: The filing provides qualitative risk disclosure, but not a forecast of actual debt-service cash outflows, refinancing probability, or the effect on specific financial ratios.

The filing also says that on certain U.S. dollar fixed-rate notes, interest rate swaps are used to effectively convert fixed rates to floating rates, and on certain foreign-currency notes, cross-currency swaps are used to effectively convert them to U.S. dollar-denominated notes.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA describes its business as a full-stack accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platform company. It says its platforms combine processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services, and that these platforms address Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive markets. It also says its data-center-scale offerings use “extreme co-design,” where chips, networking, systems, software, and algorithms are holistically architected and optimized to maximize performance and scale.

NVIDIA’s manufacturing approach, as described in the filing, is to integrate its hardware and software into tightly co-designed platforms rather than selling isolated components. The filing emphasizes that its architecture unifies GPUs, CPUs, networking, CUDA, and related software stacks, and that its full-stack innovation approach enables leveraged R&D and shared technology across multiple end markets. The implied benefit of this approach is higher performance, better scale, lower power consumption, and the ability to serve several large markets with common underlying technology.

judge.label: PARTLY_RELEVANT
judge.explanation: The answer is responsive in the sense that it discusses NVIDIA’s business/platform approach and mentions benefits like performance, scale, and lower power. However, it does not accurately answer the filing’s manufacturing question. The reference evidence says NVIDIA uses a "fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy" with partners handling wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging, and the benefits are avoiding costs and risks of owning manufacturing, plus focusing resources on product design, quality assurance, marketing, and customer support. The candidate instead emphasizes full-stack/co-design and platform integration, which is only loosely related and not the specific manufacturing approach described in the evidence.

paragraphs.text: Export controls applicable to China are described as complex and tied to chip-level measures such as total processing performance, performance density, interconnect bandwidth, and memory bandwidth. NVIDIA says that under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, it is unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China’s data center market that receives approval from both the U.S. government and the Chinese government, leaving it effectively foreclosed from competing in China’s data center computing market. NVIDIA also states that the Chinese government has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and has discouraged purchasing, importing, or using NVIDIA’s data center products, including China-specific products designed to comply with U.S. export controls. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0046; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

NVIDIA also discloses that U.S. export controls have restricted GPUs and other AI-related semiconductors, may expand to networking products and high-speed interconnects, and can include license conditions that make pre-sale and post-sale support more cumbersome. The company says repeated changes in export-control rules can create compliance burdens, disrupt supply and distribution, and encourage customers and foreign governments to shift away from NVIDIA products. NVIDIA further states that future or existing licensing conditions may be burdensome, temporary, or denied, and that China could implement standards, such as compute-per-watt and memory-bandwidth requirements for data centers, in a way that prevents NVIDIA from designing products that meet them. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0041; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0047; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0048; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0049; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0050; 0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0052]

It also references broader U.S. worldwide export controls and the burdensome licensing scheme, which are supported by the reference evidence. paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says it could be hurt because, if U.S. export controls ever allowed it to return to China’s data center compute market, Chinese government actions could still prevent it from designing products that meet new China standards, limiting customers’ ability to use some data center products and causing a material adverse impact on its business, operating results, and financial condition. The filing also explains that inability to compete in China could hurt NVIDIA by reducing demand for its products, giving rivals an advantage, and making it harder to maintain or grow its business internationally. [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a:0042

judge.label: RELEVANT

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says it is exposed to legal, administrative, and regulatory proceedings, claims, demands, and investigations involving shareholder, consumer, competition, and other issues relating to its business. [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0047] [0001045810-24-000029:item-1a:0001]

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA says its indebtedness could adversely affect its financial position and cash flows from operations, and it could also prevent the company from implementing its strategy or fulfilling its contractual obligations. The company disclosed $9.7 billion in net outstanding notes due by 2060, and stated that each series of senior notes must be repaid or refinanced when it matures unless it is redeemed or repurchased. The company said these obligations could increase vulnerability to adverse economic, industry, and competitive conditions, limit flexibility in changing its business, impair access to future financing, and restrict actions such as granting liens, entering certain mergers, disposing of assets, or materially changing its business. A covenant breach without a waiver could cause outstanding indebtedness to become immediately due and payable.

paragraphs.text: The company says its direct exposure to foreign exchange rate fluctuations is minimal because substantially all of its sales are denominated in U.S. dollars, and it uses foreign currency forward contracts to offset movements in foreign exchange rates. It also says gains or losses from foreign currency remeasurement are included in other income or expenses, and that the impact of foreign currency transaction gains or losses on net income was not significant in fiscal years 2026 and 2025.

The company further states that sales and arrangements with third-party manufacturers are priced and paid in U.S. dollars, so they are not subject to exchange rate fluctuations. It notes that a stronger U.S. dollar could make its products more expensive and hurt competitiveness, while a weaker U.S. dollar could cause suppliers to raise manufacturing costs.

On a sensitivity basis, the company estimates that a 10% strengthening of the U.S. dollar would have had an adverse impact of $180 million and $136 million, before tax, on accumulated other comprehensive income related to foreign exchange contracts as of January 25, 2026 and January 26, 2025, respectively. It also estimates that a 10% adverse foreign exchange rate change applied to balance sheet hedging contracts would have reduced income before taxes by $124 million and $129 million, respectively, with these effects expected to be offset by corresponding changes in the fair values of the underlying foreign currency denominated monetary assets and liabilities if the hedge contracts fully cover those balances.

judge.label: RELEVANT
